**Source:** Wikipedia, "Bad Habit (Steve Lacy song)," https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Habit_(Steve_Lacy_song), with the underlying sources noted below.

**Background and writing**
- Lacy signed with RCA Records in 2021 and first recorded "Bad Habit" that June, using a beat and drums he had used before. He called writing it a turning point, describing "the start of this renaissance of the separation between [past] Steve and [present] Steve" (GQ, Jeremy Gordon, June 23, 2022, https://www.gq.com/story/gq-hype-steve-lacy).
- After Lacy played the instrumental for Fousheé, the two freestyled for about 20 minutes, which produced the verses and chorus melody. Over the next year, Lacy changed the ending breakdown, drums, and chorus.
- Diana Gordon wrote part of the ending. John Carroll Kirby and Matthew Castellanos are also credited as co-writers.
- Lacy said the song was finished a week before he submitted *Gemini Rights* to RCA (Guardian, Shaad D'Souza, Dec. 22, 2022, https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/dec/22/my-mom-thinks-im-doing-drugs-but-im-at-home-baking-cookies-steve-lacy-on-his-breakout-year).
- Tyler, the Creator suggested a change to the chorus to make it "more memorable" (Billboard, Cydney Lee, Aug. 3, 2022, https://www.billboard.com/music/features/steve-lacy-bad-habit-billboard-august-2022-chartbreaker-interview-1235121728/). Lacy then altered the chorus wording.

**Recording credits** (from *Gemini Rights* liner notes)
- Steve Lacy: songwriting, production, bass
- John Carroll Kirby: songwriting, additional synths
- Brittany Fousheé, Diana Gordon, Matthew Castellanos: songwriting
- Mixed by Neal Pogue at Hot Purple Petting Zoo (Los Angeles); mastered by Mike Bozzi at Bernie Grundman Mastering.

**Release**
- Released June 29, 2022, by RCA Records as the second single from *Gemini Rights*, which came out July 15, 2022.

**Sped-up version and TikTok**
- The song went viral on TikTok starting in July 2022 and was used in over 710,000 videos by January 2023.
- Fan-made sped-up versions spread widely, one of which appeared in over 430,000 videos. RCA then released an official sped-up version. Lacy initially found the idea "gross" but agreed, hoping it would help the song reach No. 1 on the Hot 100 (Guardian, as above).

**Chart highlights**
- Debuted on the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 100 in July 2022, Lacy's first chart entry.
- Reached No. 1 on the Hot 100 in October 2022, ending "As It Was" by Harry Styles's 15-week run.
- Became the first song to top both the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and Hot Rock & Alternative Songs charts, and the first to top five Billboard genre charts at once.
- Peaked at No. 3 in Australia, No. 8 in the UK, and in the top 10 in Ireland.

**Lacy's workflow (journalist narration, para 1 and "The Real Thing")**
- *Steve Lacy's Demo* (2017) was made entirely on an iPhone, using GarageBand to edit.
- *Apollo XXI* (2019) was done by Lacy alone, including mixing.
- *Gemini Rights* (2022) involved more outside help: co-writers, producers, musicians, an engineer, and a big-name mixer.
- The article does not name Lacy's DAW for *Bad Habit*.

**Song construction**
- Journalist narration (intro): the track has "messy-sounding drums," a heavy bass, a repetitive guitar part, vocals mixed relatively far back, and a "chaotic breakdown at the end."
- The article does not say whether drums were reused or how the ending was built.

**Mix decisions (Pogue quotes, para 4 and para 5)**
- Lacy "wants his vocals in a certain space, not too loud" (para 4).
- Pogue says "The focus of 'Bad Habit' is the main guitar, and everything else supports that" (para 4).
- He calls the groove "the glue that keeps it all together" (para 4).
- Mix order: drums, then bass, then guitars, then keys, then vocals and harmonies (para 4).
- Kick: Waves SSL EQ first (para 5).
- Bass: UAD Fairchild compressor, then Waves SSL EQ, then the Waves SSL EV2 plug-in with McDSP CB101 (para 5).
- Lead vocal: UAD Fairchild 670, then Waves API 550A and SSL Channel, then Soundtoys MicroShift (para 5).
- Master bus: Waves L2 and iZotope Ozone (para 5). Mastering was by Mike Bozzi at Bernie Grundman.

**Comparison with *Apollo XXI***
- The article does not compare *Bad Habit* directly with *Apollo XXI* on sound or mixing.
- It notes that Lacy mixed *Apollo XXI* himself, while *Gemini Rights* had a professional mixer (Pogue).

**Pogue's views on the album (para 4)**
- Pogue says: "I look at an album as a TV series, and each song as a different episode."
- Client notes on *Gemini Rights* were minimal. Lacy asked for more guitar and less vocal, which surprised Pogue.

**C1. 작품 설명 — 이별 이후** [직접 발언·원문 확인] (S1)
- Lacy의 발언: "Gemini Rights is essentially me coming into myself after a breakup."
- 같은 인터뷰에서 이 이야기를 "way more hopeful"이라 하고, 핵심을 "finding happiness"로 설명합니다.
- 이 앨범에서 얻은 가장 큰 깨달음으로 "trusting my instincts"를 꼽았습니다.
- 한계: 창작자의 자기 설명입니다. 작품이 그렇게 실현됐는지에 대한 근거는 아닙니다.

- 전작과 이번 작업의 차이(S2):
  - *Apollo XXI*는 "in, like, two or three months" 만들었고 "hectic time"이었다고 말합니다.
  - 이번 앨범은 "I took my time"이라 하고, "in the studio, rather than different Airbnbs or in my home" 만들었다고 말합니다.
- 스튜디오 작업(S3):
  - "I love The Village", "I was there for two months straight"
  - "this album was me letting go of a certain process"
- 한계: "두 달"이 전체 제작 기간인지 특정 체류 기간인지는 원문에서 분명하지 않습니다. C5의 Bad Habit 경위(2021년 6월 첫 녹음, 약 1년간 수정)와 함께 놓고 보면 전체 기간은 미확정입니다.

  - Lacy는 보컬을 "not too loud" 두기를 원했습니다.
